title: How to Center a Div in Tailwind CSS | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Center a Div Instantly with Tailwind Flexbox
metaDescription: Learn how to perfectly center a div vertically and horizontally using Tailwind CSS flexbox utility classes. Adjust parameters in real-time.
explanationText: To center an element perfectly inside a parent container using Tailwind CSS, combine 'flex' with 'justify-center' (horizontal alignment) and 'items-center' (vertical alignment). Ensure the parent container has a defined height (like 'h-screen' or 'min-h-full') so vertical centering is visible.

sections.h2: The one-liner: flex, items-center, and justify-center
body: The fastest way to center a div both horizontally and vertically in Tailwind CSS is three utility classes on the parent element: flex, items-center, and justify-center. Then give the parent a height — min-h-screen for the full viewport — so there is vertical space to center within.

justify-center centers children along the main (horizontal) axis, and items-center centers them along the cross (vertical) axis. Used together they place the child in the exact middle of the container.

code.label: Vanilla CSS

body: The most common reason a div refuses to center vertically is that its parent has no height. A flex container is only as tall as its content by default, so items-center has no spare vertical space to work with. Give the parent an explicit height and the child snaps to the middle.
Use min-h-screen for a full-viewport section, h-full when the parent already sits inside a sized ancestor, or a fixed height like h-96 for a self-contained box.

When you only need one direction, drop the utility for the axis you do not care about. Horizontal only: use flex justify-center. Vertical only: use flex items-center together with a parent height. A single block that has a width: mx-auto centers it horizontally with no flexbox at all.

CSS Grid offers an even shorter route. grid place-items-center centers children on both axes in a single utility — no separate justify and items classes needed. For one centered child it behaves identically to the flex version, so the choice comes down to preference.
The parent has no height. Vertical centering needs vertical space — add min-h-screen or a fixed height to the container.
Using text-center for a block. text-center only centers inline content and text, not a block-level child element.
Putting the alignment on the child. flex, items-center, and justify-center belong on the parent container, not on the element you want centered.
Forgetting flex or grid. The alignment utilities do nothing until the container is a flex or grid context.

faq.q: How do I center a div horizontally and vertically in Tailwind CSS?
faq.a: Put flex items-center justify-center on the parent element and give it a height such as min-h-screen. items-center handles vertical centering and justify-center handles horizontal centering.

faq.q: Why is items-center not centering my div vertically?
faq.a: Because the flex container has no extra vertical space. A flex parent is only as tall as its content unless you set a height. Add min-h-screen, h-full, or a fixed height and vertical centering works.

faq.q: How do I center a div without flexbox?
faq.a: Use grid place-items-center on the parent to center on both axes, or mx-auto on a block element that has a defined width to center it horizontally only.

faq.q: What is the difference between place-items-center and items-center?
faq.a: place-items-center is a CSS Grid shorthand that sets both align-items and justify-items at once. items-center only sets cross-axis alignment and is used with flexbox alongside justify-center.

body: A responsive header is just one flex row. flex items-center justify-between pins the first child to the left edge and the last child to the right edge, while items-center keeps them on the same vertical line. Drop your logo in first and your nav or call-to-action last, and the split is done — no floats, no absolute positioning.

faq.q: Why is my navbar logo not vertically aligned with the links?

title: Sticky Footer Layout in Tailwind CSS | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Pin a Footer to the Bottom with Tailwind Flexbox
metaDescription: Stop footers from floating mid-page. Use flex-col with justify-between in Tailwind CSS to pin footers to the viewport bottom on short pages.
explanationText: A sticky footer keeps your footer pinned to the bottom of the viewport even when page content is short. Apply 'flex flex-col justify-between min-h-screen' to your page wrapper: the column direction stacks header, main, and footer vertically, and 'justify-between' pushes the first child to the top and the last child to the bottom. Alternatively, put 'flex-1' on the main content area to make it absorb all spare space.

sections.h2: The sticky footer pattern: flex-col, min-h-screen, flex-1
body: A sticky footer sits at the bottom of the viewport on short pages and below the content on long ones. Make the page wrapper a full-height column with flex flex-col min-h-screen, then give the main content flex-1 so it expands to fill any leftover space, pushing the footer down.

code.label: Vanilla CSS

body: min-h-screen maps to 100vh, which on phones can include the area under the browser toolbar and cause a slight jump as the bar shows and hides. Tailwind also ships min-h-dvh (dynamic viewport height): it tracks the visible viewport in real time, so the footer stays put. Prefer min-h-dvh for app-like mobile layouts.

sections.h2: flex vs grid for a sticky footer
body: Grid does the same job with a three-row template: grid grid-rows-[auto_1fr_auto] min-h-dvh sizes the header and footer to their content while the middle 1fr row absorbs the slack. Flex is the more common choice, but grid is tidy when you already know the header / body / footer structure.
Using position: fixed on the footer. A fixed footer overlaps content and is always visible — not the same as a sticky footer that follows the content.
No height on the wrapper. Without min-h-screen or min-h-dvh there is nothing for flex-1 to fill.
Putting flex-1 on the footer. It belongs on the main content region, which should grow — not the footer.

faq.q: How do I keep a footer at the bottom on short pages in Tailwind?
faq.a: Wrap the page in flex flex-col min-h-screen (or min-h-dvh) and add flex-1 to the main content so it expands and pushes the footer to the bottom.

faq.q: What is the difference between min-h-screen and min-h-dvh?
faq.a: min-h-screen is 100vh; min-h-dvh is the dynamic viewport height that adjusts as the mobile browser toolbar appears and disappears, avoiding layout jumps on phones.

faq.q: Should I use flex or grid for a sticky footer?
faq.a: Both work. Flex uses flex flex-col with flex-1 on main; grid uses grid-rows-[auto_1fr_auto]. Pick whichever matches the rest of your layout.

If your cards stopped matching heights, check whether an 'items-start' or 'items-center' utility crept onto the parent.

faq.q: Why are my Tailwind cards different heights?

faq.q: How do I align a button to the bottom of each card?

title: Vertical Stack Layout with flex-col in Tailwind CSS | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Stack Elements Vertically with Tailwind flex-col
metaDescription: Stack children top-to-bottom with consistent spacing using Tailwind's flex-col and gap utilities. Preview the vertical rhythm live.
explanationText: 'flex flex-col' rotates the main axis so children stack top-to-bottom, and 'gap-4' inserts identical spacing between every child without the margin-collapsing headaches of 'space-y-*' or manual margins. This is the cleanest pattern for form fields, settings lists, and any single-column mobile layout. Remember that in column mode, 'justify-*' now controls vertical distribution and 'items-*' controls horizontal alignment.

body: flex flex-col turns a container's main axis vertical, so children stack top to bottom. Add gap-4 and every child gets identical spacing between it and the next — the modern replacement for margins between stacked elements.

code.label: Tailwind

body: Tailwind offers two ways to space a stack: gap-4 (a real flex or grid gap) and space-y-4 (margins between children). Prefer gap — it never collapses, it works the same in flex and grid, and it leaves no stray margin on the first or last child. Reach for space-y-* only on plain block layouts that are not flex or grid.

The axis swap catches people out. In a column, justify-* now controls vertical distribution and items-* controls horizontal alignment. So items-center centers the stack left-to-right, and justify-center centers it top-to-bottom (given the parent has a height).
Expecting justify-center to center horizontally. In a column the main axis is vertical, so it centers vertically; use items-center for horizontal.
Mixing gap and space-y. Pick one; together they double the spacing.
Forgetting flex. flex-col does nothing until the container is a flex context.

faq.q: How do I stack divs vertically in Tailwind?
faq.a: Use flex flex-col on the parent and gap-4 for even spacing between the stacked children.

faq.q: Should I use gap or space-y for vertical spacing?
faq.a: Prefer gap. It does not collapse margins, works in both flex and grid, and never leaves a trailing margin. Use space-y only for non-flex block layouts.

faq.q: Why does justify-center not center my column horizontally?
faq.a: In flex-col the main axis is vertical, so justify-center centers vertically. Use items-center for horizontal centering in a column.

title: 3 Column Grid Layout in Tailwind CSS | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Build a 3-Column Grid with Tailwind CSS
metaDescription: Create a clean three-column grid with grid-cols-3 and gap utilities in Tailwind CSS. Adjust columns, rows, and gutters visually.
explanationText: 'grid grid-cols-3 gap-6' creates three equal-width columns ('repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))' under the hood) with consistent gutters in both directions. Children flow into cells automatically, left to right, wrapping to a new row every three items — no manual row management needed. The 'minmax(0, 1fr)' Tailwind generates is important: it lets long content shrink instead of blowing out the column width.

body: grid grid-cols-3 gap-6 creates three equal-width columns and fills them left to right, wrapping to a new row every third item. Under the hood Tailwind generates repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)), so the columns share the width evenly.

code.label: Vanilla CSS

body: Three columns are too tight on phones. Start with one column and step up at breakpoints: grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3. Each prefix only changes the column count at that width, and the gap stays consistent throughout.

sections.h2: Spanning cells and the minmax(0, 1fr) trick
body: Make one cell wider with col-span-2. And if a long word or a wide image ever blows a column out, that is exactly what the minmax(0, 1fr) Tailwind emits prevents — the 0 minimum lets a column shrink below its content size instead of overflowing. Add min-w-0 to a stubborn child if text still refuses to wrap.
Using flex for strict equal columns. Flex sizes to content unless you add basis utilities; grid columns are equal by default.
Skipping responsive prefixes. Three columns on a phone are unreadable — start at grid-cols-1.
A child overflowing its track. Add min-w-0 so long content can shrink and wrap.

faq.q: How do I make a 3 column grid in Tailwind?
faq.a: Use grid grid-cols-3 gap-6 on the container; children flow into three equal columns automatically.

faq.q: How do I make a 3 column grid responsive?
faq.a: Use grid-cols-1 on mobile and add breakpoint prefixes like sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 to increase the column count on larger screens.

faq.q: Why is my grid column overflowing its width?
faq.a: A child's content is wider than the track. Tailwind's minmax(0, 1fr) usually handles this; if not, add min-w-0 to the child so it can shrink and wrap.

title: Right Align a Button with Tailwind CSS Flexbox | Flexr Layout Lab
metaDescription: Push buttons to the right edge of a container using Tailwind's justify-end — the modern replacement for float: right. Preview it live.
explanationText: Wrap the button in a 'flex justify-end' container to push it (and any siblings) to the right edge — the modern replacement for 'float: right'. This is the standard pattern for dialog action rows and form submit areas. Need one element left and the button right instead? Switch to 'justify-between', or keep 'justify-end' and add 'mr-auto' to the element that should stay on the left.

body: Wrap your buttons in a flex justify-end container and they sit against the right edge — the modern replacement for float: right. Add gap-3 to space multiple buttons.

For a toolbar with a title on the left and a button on the right, keep flex and add ml-auto to the right-hand button. It soaks up the free space and slides itself to the edge — no justify-between needed.

The flex justify-end gap-3 pattern is the standard for modal and form footers, with Cancel next to Save. If you want the destructive action kept far from the safe one, add mr-auto to it so it stays on the left while the rest group on the right.
Reaching for float: right. It is legacy, needs clearfixes, and does not vertically align — flexbox replaces it.
Using text-right. That only affects inline text, not a block-level button.
Forgetting the container must be flex. justify-end and ml-auto both need a flex parent.

faq.q: How do I right align a button in Tailwind?
faq.a: Put it in a flex justify-end container, or add ml-auto to the button inside an existing flex row.

faq.q: What replaces float: right in Tailwind?
faq.a: Flexbox. Use flex justify-end on the parent, or ml-auto on the element you want pushed to the right.

faq.q: How do I align one button left and one right?
faq.a: Use a flex row and add ml-auto to the button that should sit on the right; the other stays on the left.

This works for logos in cards, avatars in list rows, and hero illustrations. If you only need horizontal centering, 'flex justify-center' alone does it — or use 'mx-auto' on the image itself with 'block'.

body: Images are inline elements, so old centering tricks are unreliable. The dependable fix is to make the image's parent a centering flex container: flex items-center justify-center. The image then sits dead-center regardless of its size — just give the parent a height so the vertical part has room.

faq.q: How do I center and crop an image to a fixed size?

title: Responsive Wrapping Cards with Tailwind flex-wrap | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Build Responsive Wrapping Cards with Tailwind flex-wrap
metaDescription: Let cards reflow onto new lines on small screens with Tailwind's flex-wrap and gap utilities. Resize the preview to test the breakpoints.
explanationText: 'flex flex-wrap gap-6' gives you a card row that gracefully reflows: when the container runs out of horizontal room, overflowing cards wrap onto a new line while keeping identical gutters in both directions. Unlike a rigid grid, each row packs as many cards as fit. Give each card a flex-basis (like 'basis-64') to control the wrap point, and the layout adapts to any screen width with zero media queries.

body: By default flex items refuse to wrap and shrink to fit. Add flex-wrap and, when the row runs out of horizontal room, overflowing cards drop onto a new line instead. With gap-6 the spacing stays identical in both directions.

Forgetting flex-wrap. Without it, cards squish onto one line instead of wrapping.
No basis. Cards collapse to their content width and wrap unpredictably.
Using margins instead of gap. Margins produce uneven spacing once items wrap onto multiple rows.

faq.q: How do I make cards wrap to the next line in Tailwind?
faq.a: Add flex-wrap to the flex container; cards that do not fit move to a new line automatically.

faq.q: How do I build a responsive card grid without media queries?
faq.a: Use flex flex-wrap with basis-64 grow on each card; they pack as many per row as fit and reflow as the width changes.

faq.q: Should I use flex-wrap or grid for cards?
faq.a: Use flex-wrap for a fluid, content-sized gallery; use grid grid-cols-* when you want a fixed number of equal columns at each breakpoint.

title: Two Column Layout in Tailwind CSS | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Create a Two-Column Layout with Tailwind Grid
metaDescription: Split content into two equal columns with Tailwind's grid-cols-2 — perfect for text/image splits and settings pages. Preview and copy the code.
explanationText: 'grid grid-cols-2 gap-8' is the fastest route to a balanced two-column split for text/image sections, comparison panels, or settings pages. Both columns get exactly half the available width regardless of their content, which flexbox does not guarantee without extra 'basis' utilities. To stack the columns on mobile, prefix the column count with a breakpoint: 'grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2'.

body: grid grid-cols-2 gap-8 splits a container into two equal columns and drops the first two children side by side. Each column is exactly half the width regardless of its content — something plain flexbox will not guarantee without extra basis utilities.

code.label: Vanilla CSS

body: Two columns are cramped on phones. Begin with a single column and split at a breakpoint: grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2. Below md the two blocks stack; at md and up they sit side by side.

For a wide content area beside a narrow sidebar, use fractional tracks: grid-cols-[2fr_1fr] gives the first column twice the width of the second. Or follow the 12-column convention with grid-cols-3 and col-span-2 for the main area.
Using flex without basis. Flex columns size to content, not to half each; grid gives true equal halves.
Forgetting the mobile stack. Start at grid-cols-1 and split at a breakpoint.
Fighting for equal heights. Grid rows already align both columns — no extra work needed.

faq.q: How do I make a two column layout in Tailwind?
faq.a: Use grid grid-cols-2 gap-8 on the container; the first two children become equal side-by-side columns.

faq.q: How do I stack two columns on mobile?
faq.a: Start with grid-cols-1 and add md:grid-cols-2 so the columns stack below the md breakpoint and split above it.

faq.q: How do I make one column wider than the other?
faq.a: Use fractional tracks like grid-cols-[2fr_1fr], or grid-cols-3 with col-span-2 on the wider column.

title: Evenly Spaced Links with justify-evenly in Tailwind | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Space Links Evenly with Tailwind justify-evenly
metaDescription: Distribute footer links or icon rows with perfectly equal spacing using Tailwind's justify-evenly. Compare it live against between and around.
explanationText: 'justify-evenly' distributes children so the space before, between, and after every item is identical — visually calmer than 'justify-between' (which pins the outer items to the edges) and more balanced than 'justify-around' (which halves the outer spacing). It is the right pick for footer link rows, social icon strips, and bottom tab bars. Toggle between the three in the playground above to see the difference instantly.

body: Use the justify-evenly utility class to space elements evenly across the main axis. It places equal space before the first item, between every pair, and after the last item, keeping a row of links or icons perfectly balanced at any container width.
Add it to a flex row and every child gets the same breathing room on both sides.

The three distribution utilities differ only in their edge spacing. justify-between puts zero space outside the first and last items, so they touch the edges. justify-around gives the outer items half the spacing of the inner gaps. justify-evenly makes every space — including the outer two — exactly equal. For a balanced footer or tab bar, justify-evenly reads the cleanest.
For a link row that should reflow on small screens while staying evenly spaced, combine flex flex-wrap justify-evenly gap-y-2. Items wrap onto new lines and each line stays evenly distributed.
Expecting a fixed gap. justify-evenly distributes free space, so it does nothing once items fill the row — add gap for a guaranteed minimum.
Using it on a non-flex element. It needs a flex (or grid) container.
Confusing it with justify-between. Between pins items to the edges; evenly pads the edges too.

faq.q: What does justify-evenly do in Tailwind?
faq.a: It distributes flex items so the space before, between, and after every item is identical, keeping a row perfectly balanced.

faq.q: What is the difference between justify-evenly, justify-between, and justify-around?
faq.a: justify-between puts no space at the outer edges, justify-around gives the edges half spacing, and justify-evenly makes every gap equal including the edges.

faq.q: How do I space links evenly in a Tailwind footer?
faq.a: Put the links in a flex row and add justify-evenly; add flex-wrap if they should reflow on small screens.

title: Baseline Align Mixed Text Sizes in Tailwind CSS | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Align Mixed-Size Text on One Baseline with Tailwind
metaDescription: Sit a big stat and its small label on the same text baseline with Tailwind's items-baseline — the fix for wobbly pricing and metric rows.
explanationText: When a row mixes font sizes — a large price next to '/month', or a big metric next to its unit — 'items-center' makes the text look misaligned because it centers boxes, not letters. 'items-baseline' aligns children on their text baselines instead, so every character sits on the same invisible line the way typography intends. This is the single most-missed utility in pricing tables and stat rows.

sections.h2: items-baseline lines up letters, not boxes
body: When a row mixes font sizes — a large number beside a small label — items-center looks wrong because it centers each child's box, not its text. items-baseline aligns children on their text baselines instead, so every character sits on the same invisible line the way typography intends.

body: Pricing tables ($29 next to /month), stat blocks (a big metric beside its unit), and headings with a trailing tag all read better on a shared baseline. Any time one piece of text is visibly larger than its neighbour, reach for items-baseline.

Use items-center when children are similar in size or are non-text elements like icons and avatars — it centers their boxes. Use items-baseline specifically when the meaning comes from text sitting on one line. They are not interchangeable; the right choice depends on whether you are aligning boxes or letters.
Using items-center for mixed-size text. Boxes center, but the letters look misaligned.
Applying items-baseline to icon rows. Icons have no text baseline and can align oddly; use items-center there.
Forgetting it is a parent utility. items-baseline goes on the flex container, not the text spans.

faq.q: How do I align text of different sizes on the same line in Tailwind?
faq.a: Use items-baseline on the flex row so the characters sit on a shared baseline instead of centering each box.

faq.q: What is the difference between items-baseline and items-center?
faq.a: items-center centers each child's box; items-baseline aligns children on their text baselines. Use baseline for mixed-size text and center for similar-size or non-text elements.

faq.q: Why does my price and its /month label look misaligned?
faq.a: They are probably using items-center. Switch the row to items-baseline so the large price and small label share a baseline.

title: Vertically Center Content in Tailwind CSS | Flexr Layout Lab
h1: Vertically Center Anything with Tailwind items-center
metaDescription: Vertically center icons, text, and badges inside a row with Tailwind's items-center — the flexbox answer to vertical-align. Try it live.
explanationText: The old 'vertical-align' property never worked the way anyone expected. In flexbox, vertical centering inside a row is one utility: 'items-center' on the parent aligns every child to the vertical middle of the tallest item. This is the fix for icons that sit too high next to text, badges that hug the top of a list row, and avatars that refuse to line up with usernames. Children keep their natural left-packed order because 'justify-start' stays untouched.

body: The old CSS vertical-align property only ever worked on inline and table-cell elements, which is why it so rarely did what you wanted. In a flex row the answer is one utility on the parent: items-center aligns every child to the vertical middle of the tallest one.

code.label: Tailwind
code.src: Label sits centered next to the icon

body: items-center is the cure for icons that float above their text, badges that hug the top of a list row, and avatars that will not line up with a username. Because it only touches the cross axis, the row keeps its natural left-to-right order — justify-start stays untouched.

sections.h2: Centering a row vs centering a whole container
body: There is a difference between vertically centering items within a row and centering a block inside a tall container. For a single icon-and-text line, items-center alone is enough — the row is only as tall as its content. To center a card inside a full-height section you also need a parent height (see centering a div). Same utility, different amount of vertical space.
Still reaching for vertical-align. It does not affect flex children; use items-center.
Setting self-center on every child. One items-center on the parent is simpler than repeating self-center.
Expecting it to add height. items-center aligns within the existing row height; it does not create vertical space.

faq.q: How do I vertically center items in a row in Tailwind?
faq.a: Add items-center to the flex row; every child aligns to the vertical middle of the tallest item.

faq.q: What is the Tailwind equivalent of vertical-align?
faq.a: For flex layouts it is items-center on the parent, or self-center on a single child. The vertical-align property itself only affects inline and table-cell content.

faq.q: Why is my icon higher than the text next to it?
faq.a: The flex row is missing items-center, so children align to the top. Adding items-center lines the icon up with the text's middle.

title: Tailwind flex-col-reverse: Reverse Column Order Fast
h1: Reverse Stacking Order with Tailwind flex-col-reverse
metaDescription: Learn how to use Tailwind flex-col-reverse to flip column order and build bottom-anchored chat layouts instantly with working code examples.
explanationText: 'flex-col-reverse' stacks children bottom-to-top: the first element in your DOM renders at the bottom of the container. Chat threads and activity feeds use this so the newest message stays visually anchored at the bottom while you append to the end of the list — and as a bonus, the browser keeps the scroll position pinned there. Note that only the visual order flips; screen readers and tab order still follow the DOM.

body: flex flex-col-reverse stacks children bottom to top: the first element in your markup renders at the bottom of the container. It is the go-to for chat threads and activity feeds, where you append the newest message to the end of the list but want it shown at the bottom.

sections.h2: Why the scroll stays pinned to the bottom
body: A bonus of flex-col-reverse: the browser anchors the scroll position to the bottom. Append a new message and the view stays pinned to the latest one, with no scroll-to-bottom JavaScript — exactly the behaviour a chat window wants.

sections.h2: Flexbox reversal vs CSS Grid reversal
body: This guide covers Flexbox column structures — flipping the stacking order inside a flex container. Reversing a CSS Grid is a different mechanism built on order-* utilities, grid-flow-*, and an rtl direction rather than flex-col-reverse.
If you are trying to reverse grid rows or columns, head to Reversing Item Order in Tailwind CSS Grid instead.

flex-col-reverse changes the visual order, not the DOM order — screen readers and keyboard tab order still follow the source. Keep your markup in logical reading order and let the utility handle presentation, so assistive tech announces messages sensibly.

faq.q: How do I reverse column order in Tailwind?
faq.a: Use flex flex-col-reverse on the container; children stack bottom to top, so the first element in the DOM appears at the bottom.

faq.q: How do I keep a chat scrolled to the newest message?
faq.a: flex-col-reverse anchors the scroll to the bottom, so appending a new message keeps the latest one in view without extra JavaScript.

faq.q: Does flex-col-reverse change tab order?
faq.a: No. It only flips the visual order; the DOM order, tab order, and screen-reader order stay as written.
